findings.detail: Source describes Darren giving the bully Jesse a taste of his own medicine: Darren was bullying a bully. Russian reverses the perspective and makes an unnamed bully target an ex-bully. Restore who is acting and who is being mocked.

source_anchor.quote: He was bullying a bully after all.

translation_anchor.quote: В конце концов, это задира наезжал на другого бывшего задиру.

findings.detail: «Bigots» here refers to prejudiced/intolerant people; «фанатики» suggests fanatics and is not a faithful broad rendering in the coach's anti-discrimination statement.

source_anchor.quote: We will not have bigots or racists of any kind on this team.

translation_anchor.quote: В моей команде не будет места ни фанатикам, ни расистам.

findings.detail: The source separates three complete words for emphatic delivery. Russian gratuitously splits syllables into «Яс. Но. Вы. Ра. Зил. Ся?», producing accidental unnatural comic effect. Keep emphatic separated words instead.

translation_anchor.quote: Яс. Но. Вы. Ра. Зил. Ся?

findings.detail: The reply loses the familiar vocative «man» and becomes somewhat flatter; retain its friendly informal address.
